leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members prefer the optical lattice clock for Katori and Ye, and all four write the citation around the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and uncertainties near 1e-18. The other four members (danielsson-ulf, eriksson-olle, mehlig-bernhard, olsson-eva) list B053 as an alternative, so it is the only candidate that every member either prefers or names as a fallback. What is not shared is its standing: its supporters call it mature and cleanly attributed, while several members, including its supporters, ask whether a metrology advance resting on the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes is a discovery or invention of the same standing as a new window on nature. Citation emphasis also differs slightly: Johansson would rest it on fundamental-physics reach (redshift tests, varying constants), Lindroth on the lattice scheme and neutral-atom statistics, Kroll on keeping both Katori's and Ye's contributions visible.

One member prefers topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, presenting it as a theory-then-experiment arc and a durable organising principle that the 2016 prize did not recognise. Five others (eriksson-olle, johansson-goran, kroll-stefan, lindroth-eva, olsson-eva) list B013 as an alternative, but Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll and Olsson tie that to unresolved credit (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, Hasan, and the Mele versus Molenkamp or Hasan choice) and to overlap with the 2016 prize. Mehlig's trio is the one most colleagues' opening ballots used; Danielsson's opening trio included Hasan and not Mele, and he now accepts Mehlig's core as more defensible.

One member prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene for MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, citing a clean prediction-then-observation arc and no prior prize overlap. Lindroth and Mehlig list it as an alternative. Eriksson himself concedes that B053 could be ordered ahead on maturity. Pearce, Lindroth and others raise the unsettled pairing mechanism and the absence of Yuan Cao from the credited names; Eriksson regards the flat-band prediction and correlated phases as stable and reproduced.

One member prefers the experimental Higgs discovery for Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee as the unrecognised complement to the 2013 theory prize, with no maturity question. Kroll lists it as an alternative and Pearce as a second alternative. Every member who comments, including Danielsson himself, accepts the scientific case and locates the difficulty in allocating a collaboration-scale result among three of four credited names; Danielsson says he would not resist B053 if that allocation cannot be made defensible.

One member prefers aberration-corrected electron microscopy for Rose, Haider and Urban as a mature, reproduced advance with a bounded group of originators. Olsson lists B053 and B013 as alternatives, notes that only three of eight members ranked B052 at opening, and concedes she cannot show it is more transformative than the correlated-electron candidates. Others (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce) raise a physics-versus-method question and the missing STEM-corrector strand (Krivanek, Dellby, Zach).

areas_of_agreement: Every member's round-1 file treats B053 as either the preferred configuration (four members) or a named alternative (the other four), and all eight opening proposals gave the same laureate pair, Katori and Ye.
Members who comment on B046 regard its scientific importance as overwhelming and the experimental Higgs discovery as unrecognised after 2013; the stated difficulty is allocation, not merit.

Eight of eight round-1 preferred configurations are single-part prizes; none proposes a two-part or shared-field prize, and Mehlig notes that the three-person limit makes a two-part prize impractical.

Members who comment on B001 (Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, and Johansson himself) treat circuit QED as scientifically distinct from the 2025 prize but see timing and the missing Girvin and Devoret credit as obstacles; no preferred configuration includes it.

Several members state that any citation for B053 should be written around the lattice scheme and its precision realisation, so as not to overreach into ion-clock territory or subordinate either laureate.
scientific_disputes: Whether a metrology achievement (B053) or an instrument advance (B052) counts as a discovery or invention of equal standing to a new observational window (B009) or a closed fundamental question (B046); Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson, Johansson and Pearce each take a different view.

Whether B053 is sufficiently distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize on controlled single ions: Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson consider it separable via magic-wavelength lattice trapping of many atoms, while Eriksson and Mehlig flag the overlap, and Mehlig considers the lattice clock overlap closer than the 2016 prize overlap with B013.

Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize overlaps materially with B013: Mehlig says it did not cover the quantum spin Hall prediction, Z2 classification or HgTe observation, whereas Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll and Olsson count it as a real cost.

Whether B033's unsettled pairing mechanism and device variability make it premature (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce, Eriksson as a possibility) or whether the flat-band prediction and reproduced correlated phases are already stable (Eriksson).

Whether the IceCube diffuse flux and the 3 to 5 sigma source associations (B009) amount to a mature discovery or an opening window (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig lean to the latter; Pearce lists B009 as his first alternative).
attribution_disputes: B053 laureates are identical in all eight opening proposals, but Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce note that Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley and other clock groups are outside the two supplied names, and Lindroth and Kroll disagree on how to characterise Katori's proposal versus Ye's accuracy and many-body work.

B013 trio: Mehlig, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson used Kane, Mele and Molenkamp at opening, Danielsson used Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and Hasan's 3D work lie outside any three-name set.

B046: members propose Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee but Danielsson concedes Della Negra is as defensible a CMS founder as Virdee, and others note that roles at the time of the announcement are unverified.
B009: Pearce's opening configuration was Halzen and Spiering, Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson included Karle as a third, and Mehlig adds that AMANDA and Baikal figures are not covered.

B033: the three names are agreed in all seven proposals, but Yuan Cao and other moire pioneers cannot be named, and Eriksson's own opening order of names differs from Jarillo-Herrero-first orderings used by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce.
B052: Krivanek, Dellby and Zach (STEM-corrector strand) are not covered by Rose, Haider and Urban, and Olsson calls this a real, unresolved attribution problem.
maturity_disputes: B033 is the candidate most often described as early (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce, and Eriksson who would accept B053 ahead on timing), but Eriksson notes eight years of independent replication.
B009 is described as early on source identification by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig, while Pearce regards the diffuse flux above 5 sigma as secure.

B001 timing against the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is disputed: Johansson argues it is distinct, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson see a second superconducting-circuit award as a problem.

B053 is called mature and approaching a redefinition of the second by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce, though Eriksson notes the main payoff of a redefined second and tests of constants is still prospective, and Johansson says the case should not rest on redefinition.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-goran: circuit QED (B001) is his research area, he leads the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, his Chalmers colleagues work in the field and Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize; he says he should not be the deciding voice on B001 and has not made it his preferred configuration.

Olsson-eva: an experimental electron microscopist whose group uses aberration-corrected TEM, with a field and user connection to B052 (no documented tie to Rose, Haider or Urban); she says this may warrant recusal from the B052 decision or at least weighting of her first place accordingly.

Eriksson-olle: B033 and B013 are close to his research area, B052 supplies data used by materials theory, and he served as chair for the 2025 cycle, which he says may colour his view of B001; he reports no personal tie to any credited person.

Kroll-stefan: spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder (Hall's 2005 comb prize is an enabling tool for lattice clocks) and works in atomic physics and quantum optics at Lund; he sees no specific conflict with Katori or Ye but flags the proximity.

Lindroth-eva: atomic theorist with an extended collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond group and with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich; no involvement with credited names, but she discloses field proximity as possible bias towards B053.

Pearce-mark (chair): professionally close to neutrino astronomy (B009) through astroparticle instrumentation and has a CERN-based doctorate adjacent to B046; no recorded tie to IceCube, ATLAS or CMS, and no conflict apparent for B053.
Danielsson-ulf and Mehlig-bernhard: no conflict apparent.
questions_for_round2: Is the committee prepared to treat the optical lattice clock (B053) as a discovery or invention in the statutory sense despite the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and can it state in a draft citation what is new (magic-wavelength lattice trapping of many atoms and 1e-18 accuracy) without overreaching into ion-clock work?

If the committee prefers a new window on nature or a closed fundamental question over metrology, can Danielsson and Pearce each name a defensible three-person allocation for B046 and B009 (including whether Della Negra replaces Virdee or Jenni, and whether Karle joins Halzen and Spiering), or must those candidates be set aside on allocation grounds?

For B013, can members who list it as an alternative (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson) say whether the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang omission and the 2016 overlap are disqualifying, and can Mehlig state how a citation for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp would address both?

For B033, what evidence on the pairing mechanism, device variability and the absence of Yuan Cao would change the maturity judgement of Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce, and would Eriksson accept B053 ordered ahead of B033 on timing?

Given Olsson's disclosed conflict on B052 and Johansson's on B001, should the committee decide now how those recusals are handled in later rounds, and does either member's preferred or alternative ranking need to be weighted differently?
Should B001 and B052 remain under active consideration, given that no member prefers B001 and only Olsson prefers B052, or should round 2 concentrate on B053 and one or two competing candidates?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a plurality rather than a consensus: four of eight members prefer B053, and each of B013, B033, B046 and B052 is preferred by exactly one member. Because the other four members all name B053 as an alternative, the principal open issue is not whether it has support but whether members weigh clean attribution and maturity above discovery-type standing, and whether the allocation and overlap problems in B013, B033, B046 and B009 are resolvable within three names. Disclosed field proximities cluster around B001, B052, B053 and B013 and are noted for the record without any conclusion about their effect.
